We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u={x}^{2}+6\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2x, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={e}^{2x-1}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int {e}^{2x-1}\,\text{d}x=\frac{{e}^{2x-1}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ({x}^{2}+6){e}^{2x-1}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({x}^{2}+6)(\frac{{e}^{2x-1}}{2})-\int (\frac{{e}^{2x-1}}{2})(2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{({x}^{2}+6){e}^{2x-1}}{2}-\int x\,{e}^{2x-1}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\int x\,{e}^{2x-1}\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1 \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={e}^{2x-1}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int {e}^{2x-1}\,\text{d}x=\frac{{e}^{2x-1}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\,{e}^{2x-1}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(x)(\frac{{e}^{2x-1}}{2})-\int (\frac{{e}^{2x-1}}{2})(1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{x\,{e}^{2x-1}}{2}-\frac{1}{2}\int {e}^{2x-1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{x\,{e}^{2x-1}}{2}-\frac{{e}^{2x-1}}{4}+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is a constant. 

So, we get that the indefinite integral is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ({x}^{2}+6){e}^{2x-1}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{({x}^{2}+6){e}^{2x-1}}{2}-\int x\,{e}^{2x-1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{({x}^{2}+6){e}^{2x-1}}{2}-(\frac{x\,{e}^{2x-1}}{2}-\frac{{e}^{2x-1}}{4}+D) \\  & =\frac{({x}^{2}+6){e}^{2x-1}}{2}-\frac{x\,{e}^{2x-1}}{2}+\frac{{e}^{2x-1}}{4}-D \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2x-1}}{4}(2{x}^{2}-2x+13)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-D.$ 

Finally then, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{2}+6){e}^{2x-1}\,\text{d}x & ={[\frac{{e}^{2x-1}}{4}(2{x}^{2}-2x+13)]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(\frac{{e}^{2(1)-1}}{4}(2(1)^{2}-2(1)+13))-(\frac{{e}^{2(0)-1}}{4}(2(0)^{2}-2(0)+13)) \\  & =\frac{e}{4}(2-2+13)-\frac{1}{4e}(0-0+13) \\  & =\frac{13e}{4}-\frac{13}{4e} \\  & =\frac{13{e}^{2}-13}{4e}\end{aligned}
$$
